newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-SFE wheat trades spreads, pool price bets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-SFE wheat trades spreads, pool price bets.

text.p: Australian wheat futures closed steady after recovering from early weakness in a market dominated by spread trades and some betting on a pool price increase by the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) later in the day.
January 1997 edged up by 50 cents to A$166.00 in six trades while March 1997 fell by A$1.50 to A$164.00 in eight trades.
March 1997 opened at A$161.00 on spread activity rather than market weakness, said Brendan Hillary of ANZ Futures Ltd.
Two outright trades in March 1997 at A$164.00 toward the close were on bets that the AWB would increase its pool price by perhaps A$5.00 a tonne in its revision later on Monday, he said.

Hillary also pointed out that the 76 contracts left in January wheat would have to go to delivery or be traded out by Tuesday. A large total of about 400 January 1997 from open interest of 700 were expected to go to delivery, he said.
Normally less than three percent of contracts went to delivery but the limited recent cash market had opened opportunities in futures, he said.

With the Australian market still dominated by the AWB pool price, a A$5.00 rise in the pool would justify current futures prices of A$165.00-A$166.00 but an unchanged pool estimate might cause futures to drift back toward the A$160.00 level, he said.
